holidays.name: National Sardines Day
holidays.description: A salute to the tiny, silvery, oil-packed fish that has lived in pantry corners for generations. Crack open a tin and pile the sardines on toast, toss them into pasta, or eat them straight from the can with a fork. Fans say they're one of the most nutritious snacks you can get for a couple of dollars.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. Its founder is unclear, but it has become a fixture on the November calendar for tinned-fish lovers.
holidays.funFact: Sardines are named after the Italian island of Sardinia, where huge schools of the fish were once so common that the name stuck.

holidays.name: Celebrate Your Unique Talent Day
holidays.description: A day to show off the odd skill you usually keep to yourself. Juggle, do impressions, spin a basketball on one finger, or moo like a cow. Whatever your talent is, today it gets an audience.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages people to share the quirky abilities that make them one of a kind.
holidays.funFact: Guinness World Records has logged thousands of unusual talents, from balancing spoons on the body to blowing giant bubbles, so there's very likely a record category for yours.

holidays.name: D.B. Cooper Day
holidays.description: Mystery fans mark the anniversary of one of America's most famous unsolved crimes. A man calling himself Dan Cooper hijacked a Boeing 727 and then vanished into the night sky with a parachute and a bag of ransom cash. People celebrate with theories, true-crime chats, and a lot of speculation.
holidays.origin: It marks the November 24, 1971 hijacking of a Northwest Orient flight from Portland to Seattle. The hijacker demanded $200,000, got it, and jumped from the plane. He was never conclusively identified.
holidays.funFact: A news mix-up turned the name 'Dan Cooper' into 'D.B. Cooper,' and the wrong name is the one that stuck in the legend.
